title: My God, My God, to Thee I Cry
description: My God, My God, to Thee I Cry in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 11 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 184. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: My God, my God, to thee I cry, Thee on-ly would I know; Thy pu-ri-fy-ing blood ap-ply, And wash me white as snow.

lines: My God, my God, to thee I cry,
And wash me white as snow.
Touch me, and make the leper clean;
Unless thou wash my soul from sin,
I have no part in thee.
But art thou not already mine?
Tell me again my peace is made,
The debt's discharged, the ransom's paid,
Behold, for me the victim bleeds,
For me the blood of sprinkling pleads,
O why did I my Saviour leave?
How could I thy good Spirit grieve,
I forced thee first to disappear,
Ah, Lord! if thou hadst still been here,
But O, how soon thy wrath is o'er,
O could I lose myself in thee,
My humbled soul, when thou art near,
How shall a sinful worm appear,
I loathe myself when God I see,
And Christ be in my all.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
